preview: Shreyash Borde shares his Oracle interview experience for the PMD role, detailing the online assessment, technical round, tech+HR round, and selection process.
content: SHREYASH BORDE ORACLE INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE Criteria: 1. CPI: CGPA 7 or equivalent to 70% & above, no standing arrears 2. Branches: CS, IT, Electrical, EXTC, Electronics. Locations - Mumbai / Pune / Bangalore / Chennai HIRING WORKFLOW 1. Online Test 2. PPT ( Mech. Seminar Hall ) 3. Technical Interview 4. Tech + HR Interview ONLINE TEST I ) Coding questions : 1. Count the number of strictly increasing subarrays of a specified size k in an array. Eg. arr= [5,3,5,7,8] and k=3 , The answer is 2 as [3,5,7] and [5,7,8] are the answer. 2. You are given two integer arrays: ● startTimes[i] – the start time when employee i is available. ● endTimes[i] – the end time when employee i is no longer available. Each employee is available for interaction in the interval [startTimes[i], endTimes[i]]. (inclusive) Find the maximum size of a team such that at least one employee in the team can interact with all others. Ex. startTimes = [1, 2, 3, 6] endTimes = [4, 5, 7, 8] Employee 2: [3, 7] can interact with ● 0: [3, 4] ● 1: [3, 5] ● 3: [6, 7] ∴ Max team size = 4 For both there questions, I had just applied brute force method O( n2) II ) Aptitude : These were some basic table seating positions and PnC type of questions. III ) Grammar : Given a passage you would be asked some questions. IV ) CS Fundamentals : This section had OS(page faults, resource allocation), DBMS, Computer Networks(subnets) and some RESTFUL API questions. After the online assessment, ~45 students were selected for interviews. Out of which ~20 were for 1st role(OFSSA) and ~25 for 2nd(PMD). I was selected for the 2nd role. TECHNICAL INTERVIEW (~45 min) 1. Introduction - I was asked to introduce myself and my internships. He then continued asking questions based on my answers for ~15 min. My resume had Android projects so he kept on asking about the OS and Android apps/app development. 2. He then asked how passwords should be handled, so I explained to him encryption, hashing and salting. 3. The interviewer then asked whether I was comfortable in Java and then asked me to implement a stack using an array, along with push, pop and peek functions. It had been some time since I had done that so I missed the overflow/underflow conditions, but he nudged me by asking if it was my final implementation. That's when I realized my mistake and then implemented it correctly. Then, he just did a dry run with an example and asked me the time and space complexities for those functions. 4. Then he asked me about a. Linked list and ArrayList b. Sets and Trees In Java and the differences, time complexity for common operations(add, remove) and in which situation which one is better. 5. Then he asked me about the 4 pillars of OOP and asked in detail about Inheritance with method overloading and inherited methods in child classes. 6. Then I was given a table emp_id emp_name mgr_id 1 A 3 2 B 1 3 C 0 I was asked to output the name of the employee along with their manager. I could tell that SELF JOIN operation is needed, but I could not recall the correct query syntax. So, I started building the query from the right starting from the condition. I got most of it correct except some syntax error(like alias for the table) 7. Then he asked me about the different types of sorts and which one is the best. I told him about the different ones I knew(bubble, merge, selection, quick, insertion) along with their best, worst and average time complexities. 8. And then he asked if I had any questions? TECH+HR(~30min) 1. He asked me about my family background, where I live and whether I had any plans to pursue further education. After this question, all the rest were technical questions 2. He gave a 3 tier architecture with client, server and db. He asked that the client is facing high latency, how would you try to solve this. I did not have much idea about this so I told whatever I knew about it. So are all clients facing it or a few. Is it location based, etc. and said we’d need to consider stuff like network location of servers, heavy computation, etc. 3. I was given two tables s_id s_name 1 A 2 B s_id s_addr 1 Addr1 2 NULL I was asked to print the name along with the address excluding NULL. I had prepared JOINS after the 1st round, so I could solve this one pretty easily. 4. Then he asked me about the multiplatform app development(which was on my resume). I explained its advantages and disadvantages. Then he asked some questions related to my answers. 5. He then asked me about a Facial recognition project on my resume and asked about ML. He asked whether it recognized people with/without spectacle, hair or facial hair. I honestly told him the shortcomings of the model that it does not work with hair but works with spectacles and also explained to him the probable reasons and how it can be prevented. 6. And then he asked if I had any questions? For both the interviews I had asked them to tell me about some project they were proud of. An hour after this round, 12 candidates were called to the GD room, where the HR came and told us that all of us were selected for the 2nd role. Everyone was surprised(we were expecting a 3rd round which was taking place for the 1st role). She then asked some basic things like nationality. In the end, 5 were selected for 1st role and 12 for 2nd role. Tips: 1. Make sure you enter with a smile and greet them because your first impression can have a lot of impact. 2. Prepare the “Tell me about yourself” and a few common HR questions beforehand and don’t try to mug them, just remember key points and tell the answer around it because most of the time we forget the answer that we have prepared . 3. For a DSA Question, try to think out loud and share your ideas with the interviewer. If the question is not clear to you, ask the interviewer to explain it again with some test case. Resources : For final revision for this interview, I referred to https://takeuforward.org https://www.interviewbit.com
